feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 0 (five 12 mm sensors, span ±0.024 m) had 60 trials, zero completions, line-loss events of 1.0 to 1.8 per run, and max_error of 0.061 to 0.064 m, just past the 0.06 m off-track limit (cited in the iteration 0 outcome table). Iteration 1 (seven 12 mm sensors, span ±0.036 m) kept the same failure pattern, with line loss of 1.0 on the s-bend and slalom, and progress on the oval fell from 0.22 to 0.12. Iteration 1 also changed kp from 3.0 to 4.0, so that drop cannot be assigned to span alone. Iteration 2 (your 16 mm contiguous layout at ±0.048 m, kp 5.0) removed line loss on the oval and s-bend, which supports the footprint change. But s-bend progress fell to 0.04 with max_error 0.0611 m and zero line loss, so the robot now leaves the tape by drift or turn-rate lag rather than by losing sensor coverage. Your iteration 3 geometry is the same as iteration 2, and I built it with kp 5.0 to isolate gain. Use the next race to decide the next step. If line_loss_events are still above zero on the slalom, widen the pitch to 20 mm (x = -0.06 to +0.06, y = 0.03), because the 4 to 5 cm error zone is still not covered. If steering_oscillation rises above 0.16 with line_loss_events at zero, move the sensor y offset to 0.05 m. If the robot stays off track with zero line loss (as the iteration 2 s-bend did), change wheel_track to 0.10 m with mass 0.6 kg to increase turn rate; I would hold the sensor layout fixed for that test.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events stay above zero on the slalom after this race, change sensor_positions to seven 16 mm sensors at 20 mm pitch (x = -0.06 to +0.06, y = 0.03). Evidence: iterations 0, 1 and 2 each show one line-loss event per slalom run, and the 12 mm and 16 mm contiguous layouts at ±0.036 and ±0.048 m did not remove it.

If steering_oscillation rises above 0.16 with line_loss_events at zero, set the sensor y offset to 0.05 m for all sensors. Evidence: iteration 0 oscillation was 0.14 to 0.16 on the s-bend and slalom, and iteration 2 oval was 0.075, so the jitter risk is in the lateral error, not the footprint.

If the robot stays off track with zero line loss on the s-bend (max_error near 0.061 m, progress near 0.04 as in iteration 2), try wheel_track 0.10 m with mass 0.6 kg with the sensor layout unchanged. Evidence: iteration 2 s-bend had zero line loss but progress of 0.04, and iteration 0 slalom had the lowest progress (0.108) with the largest gap between rms_error and progress, which points to turn-rate limits.
